title: Rebellion Against the King
summary: Amalekites and Amulonites stirred unconverted Amalekites, Amulonites, and Lamanites to anger against their brethren. Their hatred grew; they began to rebel against their king and took up arms against the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

explicit_facts.text: The groups described as unconverted were in the lands of Amulon, Helam, and Jerusalem, and in the land round about.
Amalekites and Amulonites stirred them to anger against their brethren.
Their hatred became exceedingly sore, and they began to rebel against their king because they did not want him to be their king.
They took up arms against the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the people and their arms.
The exact place where the rebellion and taking up of arms occurred.

narration.text: therefore, they took up arms against the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The king and the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi are mentioned but are not described as physically present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle; the verses describe taking up arms, not combat.
Do not invent speeches or identify a specific place where the rebellion occurred.
Do not depict the king as physically present.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and manner of the transfer are not stated.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the king's death or the Lamanites' preparations as simultaneous with the transfer.
Do not invent a ceremony, spoken words, or a cause of death.

title: From Midian to Ishmael
summary: Ammon, his brethren, and those who had come up with him saw the Lamanites' preparations to destroy their brethren. They came to Midian, where Ammon met all his brethren. From there they came to Ishmael intending to hold a council with Lamoni and Anti-Nephi-Lehi about defending themselves against the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon, his brethren, and those who had come up with him saw the Lamanites' preparations to destroy their brethren.
They came to the land of Midian, where Ammon met all his brethren.
From Midian they came to the land of Ishmael intending to hold a council with Lamoni and his brother Anti-Nephi-Lehi about defending themselves against the Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Their movement from Midian to Ishmael can be shown as travel between the named lands, in sequence.
unspecified_visual_details: The route and appearance of either land.

title: Retain the Swords Unstained
summary: An unidentified speaker addresses brethren, urges them not to stain their swords with their brethren’s blood, and urges them to retain their swords. The speaker warns that, if they stain their swords again, they perhaps can no longer be washed bright.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker addresses the listeners as beloved brethren and says God has taken away their stains and their swords have become bright.
The speaker urges them not to stain their swords with the blood of their brethren.
The speaker urges them to retain their swords so they will not be stained with their brethren’s blood.

The speaker says that, if they stain their swords again, perhaps they can no longer be washed bright through the blood of the Son of their great God, which shall be shed for the atonement of their sins.

summary: After the king finishes speaking, the assembled people bury their swords and other weapons deep in the earth. They do this as a testimony and covenant not to use weapons again to shed blood.

They covenanted to give up their own lives rather than shed their brethren’s blood, to give to a brother rather than take from him, and to labor abundantly rather than be idle.

title: A Warning About Falling Away
summary: The verse teaches that people who have been enlightened and gained knowledge of righteousness become more hardened if they later fall into sin and transgression.

explicit_facts.text: People once enlightened by the Spirit of God and knowledgeable about righteousness become more hardened if they fall into sin and transgression; their state becomes worse than if they had never known these things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching could be presented as narration over a nonliteral background.
unspecified_visual_details: No specific people, event, location, or visible appearance of the Spirit is described.

narration.text: And thus we can plainly discern, that after a people have been once enlightened by the Spirit of God, and have had great knowledge of things pertaining to righteousness, and then have fallen away into sin and transgression, they become more hardened, and thus their state becomes worse than though they had never known these things.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a teaching, not a narrated visible transformation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Spirit as a visible figure or invent a specific fallen people.
